p.CATALOG-IS-THE-OPERATIONAL-CORE: *The operational core of "explanation capital must be runnable capital" (Manifesto §5).*

p.NINE-CLASSES-CARRY-COGNITION: *Nine classes of artifact that carry a strong author's cognition in a form a weak reader CONSUMES rather than re-derives.*

p.EACH-PATTERN-IS-ALSO-A-CARD: *Each pattern is also a card, shipped per-language in each stack's `cards/`; this catalog is the language-neutral overview and the build order.*

p.two-properties-at-once-lead: An **executable scaffold** has two properties at once:

facts.PROPERTY-RUNS-OR-MACHINE-CHECKS: **It runs or machine-checks** — compiles, executes, or evaluates as a checker, emitting a pass/fail (or typed) signal. Prose has no signal.
facts.PROPERTY-CARRIES-COGNITION: **It carries cognition** — a weak reader USES it instead of re-deriving the understanding.

p.SCAFFOLD-IS-UNDERSTANDING-WITH-A-PULSE: A scaffold is materialized understanding with a pulse.

p.empirical-basis-esolang-follow-up: **Empirical basis.** EsoLang follow-up (Jun 2026): weak agents given a *written* strategy barely moved (Sonnet 12→12); given an *executable* helper library, they leapt (12→64).

p.mechanism-not-the-idea-but-the-code: Mechanism: mid-tier models lack not the idea but the ability to build the reusable code that carries it (R2C-008).

p.TRANSFER-TAG-LEGEND: **Transfer tags.** [E-strong] = directly supported by that generation result; [E-mid] = supported by other ledger findings; [E-hyp] = first-principles, validate in pilot.

p.transfer-to-modification-is-the-pilots-j: The result is about *generation*; transfer to *modification* is the pilot's job.

p.floor-haiku-stayed-near-it: **The floor.** Even with the executable library, Haiku-4.5 stayed near the floor.

p.SCAFFOLDS-AMPLIFY-NOT-CREATE: Scaffolds amplify capability; they do not create it.

p.row-details-live-in-the-card: Each row's full Applicability/Routine/Checker is in its card.

facts.BUILD-ORDER-E: **E (fast loop)** — substrate; nothing pays off without it. First.
facts.BUILD-ORDER-G-AND-F: **G (doctests) + F (diagnostics)** — cheapest runnable capital; guaranteed-truthful few-shot signal. [E-strong].
facts.BUILD-ORDER-B-AND-C: **B (typed builders) + C (contracts)** — convert hallucinations to compile/assert failures at seams. [E-mid].
facts.BUILD-ORDER-D: **D (differential oracles)** — the modification-specific safety net; the class most worth validating for our actual task. [E-mid].
facts.BUILD-ORDER-I: **I (codemods)** — potentially decisive for the swarm, but [E-hyp]; prototype and measure before the guide commits to it.

reality-checklist.title: 3. The scaffold-reality checklist (all four must hold)

facts.CHECKLIST-RUNS-OR-CHECKS: [ ] **Runs/checks:** emits pass/fail or typed signal, not prose.
facts.CHECKLIST-CARRIES-COGNITION: [ ] **Carries cognition:** encodes a decision a weak reader would otherwise re-derive.
facts.CHECKLIST-FAST-ENOUGH: [ ] **Fast enough:** signal returns inside the per-cell loop budget (<~60s).
facts.CHECKLIST-CANNOT-SILENTLY-LIE: [ ] **Cannot silently lie:** if it drifts from reality it FAILS (compile error / assert / red test), never misleads. (The doctest-vs-comment distinction.)

build-use-boundary.title: 4. The build/use boundary (a pilot hypothesis worth stating)

p.sharp-capability-line-hypothesis: There may be a sharp capability line between *building* a scaffold (Classes A, I — emit/parameterize) and *using* one (Classes G, H — consume).

p.evidence-haiku-did-not-improve: Evidence: Haiku did not improve even with the executable library, suggesting the barrier is not the scaffold's presence but the ability to wield it.

p.WEAKEST-TIER-GETS-CONSUME-ONLY-SCAFFOLDS: If true, the weakest swarm tier should receive consume-only scaffolds (G/H) and invoke-only operations (I as a fixed command), never build-it-yourself scaffolds.
